The main takeaway from our work is that

herbivores elicit jasmonate-mediated defence responses and 12-oxophytodienoic acid and cytokinin signalling to regulate stomata and photosynthesis, respectively, and that the two pathways are integrated by mitogen-activating protein kinase 4.

herbivores can elicit changes in photosynthesis by interacting with phytohormones and that the signalling pathways regulating these responses are complex, but can be dissected by using a combination of transgenic plants, micrografting, gas exchange and phytohormonal profiling.

herbivore-specific oral secretions, in addition to inducing jasmonic acid-mediated plant defence pathways, also elicit jasmonic acid and 12-oxophytodienoic acid signalling pathways to decrease carbon assimilation, which may reduce carbon availability for herbivore growth.
